title: Assignment 7: Stop Before the Wall with ROS 2
description: Write a complete ROS 2 node in build_node() that drives forward and stops before a wall, using the readings straight ahead in a 270-degree scan.
assignment_html:
Scenario

A robot drives straight toward a wall. Write the ROS 2 node that controls it: drive forward while the way ahead is clear, and stop before the wall. If the wall moves away again, drive again. You decide how to structure the node and which scan readings to use.

What the robot gives you

  • /scan (sensor_msgs/msg/LaserScan) arrives about 12 times per second. scan.ranges holds the distances in metres (you can index it like a Python list), swept from the robot's right (−135°) to its left (+135°).
  • The middle reading, scan.ranges[len(scan.ranges) // 2], points straight ahead, so it is the distance to the wall. You may also look at a few readings on each side of it. Reading i points at scan.angle_min + i * scan.angle_increment radians.
  • A reading of positive infinity (inf) means nothing was detected within range, so the way is clear: drive. This follows the usual ROS convention (REP 117).
  • /cmd_vel (geometry_msgs/msg/Twist) moves the robot. linear.x is the forward speed in m/s; 0.0 means stop.

The rule your node must follow

  • Way clear (nothing in range, or the wall more than 1.0 m away): publish a forward speed between 0.1 and 0.3 m/s.
  • Wall 0.3 m away or closer: publish linear.x = 0.0.
  • Between 0.3 m and 1.0 m: your choice. Pick a STOP_DISTANCE above 0.3 m and at most 1.0 m (for example 0.5 m) and stop when the distance ahead is at or below it. Do not pick exactly 0.3: a reading of 0.3 m arrives as a float32 slightly above 0.3, so distance <= 0.3 would not stop for it.
  • Always: keep angular.z = 0.0 (never turn).

Press Simulate to watch your node drive a robot in a small 2D world. The robot starts 1.2 m from a wall; once it has been stopped for 1 second, the wall slides 1.5 m away so you can see whether it drives again. The simulation is only for watching: it does not change your score.

Task

Write your code in src/wall_stop/wall_stop/controller.py, inside build_node():

  1. Create your node. Either define a class that extends Node (add from rclpy.node import Node) and create an instance, or call rclpy.create_node('wall_stop'). Both are accepted.
  2. Create a Twist publisher on /cmd_vel.
  3. Subscribe to LaserScan messages on /scan with a callback function.
  4. In the callback, get the distance straight ahead from scan.ranges.
  5. In the same callback, publish one Twist: the forward speed when the way is clear, or linear.x = 0.0 when the wall is at or inside your STOP_DISTANCE.
  6. Keep the speed and the stop distance in named constants at the top of the file, such as FORWARD_SPEED = 0.2 and STOP_DISTANCE = 0.5.
  7. Return the node at the end of build_node().

Rules

  • Read the complete project tree, but edit only src/wall_stop/wall_stop/controller.py.
  • Do not change main(), and do not rename the package, executable, topics, or build_node().
  • controller.py may import only rclpy, geometry_msgs, sensor_msgs, and math.
  • Built-in functions that reach outside your node, such as open(), eval(), exec(), getattr() and vars(), are not allowed, and their names cannot be reused for your own variables.
  • Do not use a while True or while rclpy.ok() loop, sleep() or sleep_for(), and do not spin inside build_node(). Let the scan callback do the work.
  • Publish exactly one Twist inside the /scan callback for every scan (about 12 per second), also when the command has not changed. Do not publish from a timer.

What Run Tests checks

1. Before anything is scored. Only allowed imports; build_node() exists and main() is still there; the package builds; the node starts and publishes on /cmd_vel; build_node() returns a ROS node. If one of these fails, the score is 0.

2. Behaviour. The grader sends your node made-up scans of a flat wall straight ahead and watches /cmd_vel. No robot simulator is used. Each situation lasts 1 second (about 12 scans), and the first 0.3 s is not checked so your node has time to react. The six situations, in order:

  • Nothing in range (every reading is inf): must drive.
  • Wall 1.2 m ahead: must drive.
  • Wall 0.3 m ahead: must be stopped.
  • Wall 0.2 m ahead: must be stopped.
  • Wall still 0.2 m ahead: must stay stopped.
  • Wall back at 1.2 m: must drive again.

Drive means linear.x between 0.1 and 0.3 m/s. Stopped means linear.x within ±0.001 m/s. angular.z must stay within ±0.001 rad/s in every command, the node must publish at least 5 commands per second, and it must publish exactly one command inside the /scan callback for every scan. Distances between 0.3 m and 1.0 m are not tested. Stopping only earns credit when the robot also drives when the way is clear.

3. Code checks. A Twist publisher on /cmd_vel and a LaserScan subscription on /scan exist while the node runs; the code reads scan.ranges; there is no while True or while rclpy.ok() loop, sleep(), sleep_for() or spinning inside build_node(); main() is unchanged; the speed and the stop distance are named constants; and there are no unused imports that you added.

This is a test with made-up scans, not a real-robot safety certification.

How scoring works

Behaviour is worth 70% (nine checks), code checks 20% (five checks), and code quality 10% (two checks). The code, quality and publishing points count only once your robot passes at least one driving check, so a robot that never drives earns 0%. The untouched starter earns 0% because build_node() returns nothing. The task counts as passed when everything before scoring passes and all nine behaviour checks pass. Code and quality points add to the score but do not decide passing.

import math

import rclpy
from geometry_msgs.msg import Twist
from rclpy.executors import ExternalShutdownException
from sensor_msgs.msg import LaserScan


def build_node():
    """Create your node, connect /scan and /cmd_vel, and return the node.

    Use a class (class WallStop(Node): ...) or plain functions with
    rclpy.create_node('wall_stop'). Both are accepted.
    """
    # Write your code here.
    return None


def main(args=None):  # Do not change main().
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = build_node()
    try:
        rclpy.spin(node)
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, ExternalShutdownException):
        pass
    finally:
        node.destroy_node()
        rclpy.try_shutdown()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

solution_html:
Approach

  1. Inside build_node(), create the node, a Twist publisher on /cmd_vel and a LaserScan subscription on /scan, and return the node.
  2. In the scan callback, take a few readings around the middle of scan.ranges (the middle one points straight ahead) and skip NaN.
  3. Publish FORWARD_SPEED when the nearest of those readings is greater than STOP_DISTANCE; positive infinity counts as clear. Otherwise publish zero.
  4. Leave angular.z at 0.0 and publish once per scan, so motion resumes on the first clear scan.
